approachQuestion.prompt:
Light-map load. A rectangular panel has R rows and C columns but is supplied only as a read-only array entries of k lit cells. Each entry contains a valid zero-based row, column, and positive integer load. Cell coordinates are unique; omitted cells have load zero. Return total load over the panel. There are 1 <= R,C <= 1,000,000,000 and 0 <= k <= 200,000, with k <= R*C. Loads and the total fit signed 64-bit. Dimensions, k, and indexed entry access are directly available. Choose minimum worst-case time and then auxiliary space. The return value is one integer; no dense panel needs to be produced.

Example 1: Input: R=4,C=5,entries=[(0,2,7),(3,4,2)]. Output: 9.
Example 2: Input: R=8,C=9,entries=[]. Output: 0.

options.text: Initialize a total to zero and add the load from each supplied entry.
options.feedback: The entries contain all nonzero contributions, and unique coordinates rule out replacement or duplicate-coordinate semantics.

options.text: Allocate and zero an R-by-C panel, write each entry into its coordinate, then sum every panel cell.
options.feedback: The total is correct if enough memory exists, but most cells may be omitted. A panel with one entry can have a trillion cells; materializing them is unnecessary for a scalar sum.

options.text: Multiply k by the load in the first entry, returning zero when k is zero.
options.feedback: Loads may differ. For entries=[(0,0,2),(0,1,5)] on a 1-by-2 panel, this returns 4 instead of 7.

options.text: Add each entry’s row and column indices instead of its load.
options.feedback: Coordinates locate cells but are not their loads. A 1-by-1 panel with entry (0,0,7) has total 7, not 0.

feedback.reason: Analyze the supplied representation rather than the size of the conceptual universe it describes.
details: Start the sum at zero. Iterate entries, adding the load field of each record once. Return zero if there are no records. Do not allocate a panel or inspect omitted coordinates.

A million-by-million panel with two supplied lit cells requires two load additions, not a scan over a trillion coordinates. Omitted cells contribute zero by the representation contract. When k=0, setup and returning zero still take constant work, which is why the bound includes +1.
“Initialize a total to zero and add the load from each supplied entry.”: The entries contain all nonzero contributions, and unique coordinates rule out replacement or duplicate-coordinate semantics.

“Allocate and zero an R-by-C panel, write each entry into its coordinate, then sum every panel cell.”: The total is correct if enough memory exists, but most cells may be omitted. A panel with one entry can have a trillion cells; materializing them is unnecessary for a scalar sum.
“Multiply k by the load in the first entry, returning zero when k is zero.”: Loads may differ. For entries=[(0,0,2),(0,1,5)] on a 1-by-2 panel, this returns 4 instead of 7.
“Add each entry’s row and column indices instead of its load.”: Coordinates locate cells but are not their loads. A 1-by-1 panel with entry (0,0,7) has total 7, not 0.

complexityQuestion.prompt: For sum-sparse-records, choose worst-case time and peak auxiliary space in terms of R, C, and k. Include constant setup even for k=0. Reading a record and adding its fixed-size load take constant time; input and scalar output are excluded.
constraints: Choose the tightest standard bound for the complete execution. Count peak simultaneously live auxiliary storage; exclude supplied input and required output.
Word arithmetic, indexing, and copying one fixed-size element take constant time. No hashing or recursion is used.

feedback.reason: Traversal follows k stored records rather than the dense panel area.
details: The method performs constant setup and exactly k record visits, giving O(k+1) time, including the empty case. R and C validate the domain but do not determine the traversal. Only a total and an index remain live, with no hashing, recursive stack, copied records, or dense grid.
“O(RC + 1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: This describes visiting all conceptual cells; the actual loop visits only k records. It is loose when k is small.
“O(k + 1) time, O(RC) auxiliary space”: No grid is allocated. The supplied sparse records are input, not auxiliary storage.
“O(1) time, O(1) auxiliary space”: A load at any supplied entry can change the answer, so k record visits cannot be omitted in the worst case.
